reviewers.summary: The dashboard renders accepted trace and evidence URLs as links, but safeHref does not reject browser-equivalent protocol-relative paths.

findingList.message: The same-origin URL check can be bypassed with a backslash after the leading slash, allowing a purported trace or evidence link to navigate off-site (OWASP A01:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: safeHref accepts any string beginning with one slash; evidence and activity trace URLs that pass this check are rendered as anchor hrefs.
evidence.failureScenario: If backend data contains `/\\evil.example/x`, safeHref accepts it, but browsers treat the backslash as a slash when resolving the URL, so the link can navigate to evil.example instead of staying same-origin.

reviewers.summary: The component covers capability and activity labels, design-only cards, supplied decision actions, and inert text rendering. Queue-item labels and M-02 forged-command rejection are not covered by this change.

findingList.message: Acceptance criterion 1 requires labels for queue items as well as capabilities and activity. Queue items are absent from the dashboard data and rendering, and no test covers their labels.

evidence.codePathTraced: DashboardData contains only capabilities and activity, and CapabilityDashboard renders only those collections.
evidence.failureScenario: When the dashboard has queue items to display, this component has no queue-item data or rendering path, so those items cannot display their backend-supplied labels.

findingList.message: M-02 requires a test showing forged client permissions do not authorize an API command. The named tests cover displayed actions only; add a test that submits a forged command and verifies the API rejects it.

evidence.codePathTraced: The role-permitted decisions tests verify that supplied actions render and invoke the callback, but do not exercise an API command with forged client permissions.
evidence.failureScenario: If a client adds a disallowed action and submits its command, the tests would still pass even if the API accepted it; the M-02 authorization behavior is therefore unverified.

reviewers.summary: The UI renders supplied action data and dispatches the chosen action. The change does not verify the acceptance criterion that forged client permissions cannot authorize an API command.

findingList.message: M-02's forged-permission condition has no test proving that an unauthorized API command is rejected; the added tests cover displayed actions and callback dispatch only.

evidence.codePathTraced: The dashboard renders buttons from client-held capability.actions and passes the selected action ID to onDecision; the added tests verify role-based projection and callback dispatch but do not exercise an API command with forged client permissions.
evidence.failureScenario: A signed-in user alters the client-held action list to add a decision their role is not permitted to make. This change's tests do not establish that the resulting API command is rejected, so the M-02 authorization requirement is unverified.
